prompt: As of 2026, order these artists by how famous they are in the U.S. (share of Americans who have heard of them).
explanation: YouGov's fame ratings: Bruno Mars 94%, Drake 90%, Kendrick Lamar 83%, Kesha 78%. Bruno Mars is also much the best liked of the four (64% positive, against 49% for Kendrick, 45% for Kesha and 41% for Drake).
caveat: Fame is YouGov's measure: the share of U.S. adults who say they have heard of the artist. The ratings update over time.

prompt: As of 2026, order these four female singers by popularity in the U.S. (share of Americans with a positive opinion of them).
explanation: Dolly Parton is liked by 80% of Americans and disliked by only 3%. Taylor Swift is the best known (98% have heard of her) but only 53% view her positively, with 24% negative. Lady Gaga sits at 64% and Sabrina Carpenter at 47% (79% have heard of her).
caveat: Popularity is YouGov's share of all U.S. adults with a positive opinion, not streams or sales. It was chosen over Spotify monthly listeners because that figure is global and skews young and online; by streams, Taylor Swift would rank first.

prompt: In 2025, what percentage of U.S. adults picked Korean pop music (K-pop) when asked which parts of South Korean culture they are interested in?
explanation: 12% of U.S. adults picked Korean pop music when asked which parts of South Korean culture they are interested in. Korean food was far ahead at 42%, and 45% chose none of the options.

source.publisher: Korea Economic Institute of America / YouGov
source.title: KEI 2025 Annual Survey (Americans' attitudes on U.S.–Korea relations)

caveat: No reputable national survey of weekly K-pop listening exists, so this measures stated interest (a select-all-that-apply question), not listening frequency.

prompt: Order these genres by how much they were streamed in the U.S. in 2025 (on-demand audio streams).
explanation: R&B/hip-hop led with 349.9 billion U.S. on-demand audio streams, about a quarter of the 1.4 trillion total. Rock was second at 260.5 billion, well ahead of pop (167.2 billion) and country (122.5 billion). Latin was just behind country at 120.9 billion.

source.title: Music streams hit 5 trillion in 2025. Christian, rock and Latin lead growth in the US

caveat: Genre is Luminate's classification of each track, and rock includes a large amount of older catalog music.

prompt: In 2025, for every 100 CDs shipped in the U.S., about how many vinyl records were shipped?
explanation: Vinyl outsold CDs: 46.8 million vinyl records against 29.5 million CDs, or about 159 vinyl records per 100 CDs. Vinyl units rose 7.9% while CDs fell 11.6%, and vinyl revenue passed $1 billion.
caveat: RIAA counts units shipped by labels, not retail purchases. The 159 figure is calculated from the two unit counts.

prompt: In early 2026, what share of Americans aged 12 and older had listened to Spotify in the past month?
explanation: 36% of Americans 12+ used Spotify in the past month, the most of any online audio brand. YouTube Music was close at 34%, then Pandora at 21%, Amazon Music at 19% and Apple Music at 17%.
caveat: The base is everyone aged 12 and older, not only adults or only people who stream music.

prompt: In 2026, what percentage of U.S. adults said radio is one of the ways they listen to music?
explanation: 48% of U.S. adults say radio is one of the ways they listen to music, second only to streaming at 73%. CDs and downloaded files are each at 24%, vinyl records at 11% and cassettes at 4%.
caveat: Select-all-that-apply question about formats people use, with no time frame or frequency attached.
